chunks: Muḥammad ibn Sahl narrated from his father, from some of his shaykhs, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام was asked about a man who was sitting with a group of people and died while among them, or a man who was found in a tribe or at the house of some people, and they were accused regarding him. He said: There is no retaliation upon them, and his blood is not to be left unavenged; the blood money is upon them.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَا: The Commander of the Faithful, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Blood money paid as financial compensation
key_terms.دَمُهُ: His blood, meaning liability for the killing
key_terms.قَبِيلَةٍ: A tribe or communal group within which a dead person is found
key_terms.قَوَدٌ: Retaliatory execution or qiṣāṣ for homicide

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person is found dead among a group of people and they are accused of his killing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a suspicious death connected to a group or locality. It states that qiṣāṣ is not imposed on the accused people in such a case, but the victim’s blood is not disregarded, and the diyyah is due from them.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5177 - Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated from his father, from some of his elders, from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:

"The Commander of the Faithful (as) was asked about a man who was sitting with a group of people and died while among them, or a man who was found dead in a tribe or near the house of some people, and they were accused of his death.
Imam (as) said: 'There is no retaliation (qisas) upon them, nor is his blood wasted. However, the blood money (diyyah) is upon them.'"
